reason: The code supports an uncancellable queued request and permissionless finalization, but the report does not demonstrate that this path enables slashing or establish the claimed loss or fund-lock impact.

evidence.claim: Operators cannot cancel a queued vault-stake request to a DSS; anyone (including a malicious DSS) can finalize it after the delay, exposing funds to slashing.
evidence.support_reason: requestUpdateVaultStakeInDSS (Operator.sol:61-87) stores pendingStakeUpdates[vault] and there is no cancel function anywhere; finalizeUpdateVaultStakeInDSS (Core.sol:146-153) has no caller restriction and validateQueuedStakeUpdate (Operator.sol:89-101) only checks delay and root match, so any party can finalize the queued stake.
preconditions: operator has submitted a stake request to a DSS that later turns malicious
veto committee does not cancel the resulting slashing in time
missing_evidence: demonstration that a malicious DSS can actually slash the newly-staked vault (DSS must be registered and operator registered to it)
quantification of loss vs. the acknowledged 'sitting on queued withdraw' / DSS-should-ignore-queued-stake design note
